title: Paying to be told no
category_name: Visas, refusals and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A visa fee buys consideration, not a visa, and it is not returned when the answer is no. Nigerians are refused at rates several times the global average, and the refused fees are a measurable national transfer to the refusing states.

title: Being cut to three months, single entry
category_name: Visas, refusals and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: In July 2025 the United States reduced most non-immigrant visas for Nigerians to a single entry valid three months, replacing the five-year multiple-entry visas many held - and then suspended issuance entirely.

title: Meeting every requirement and being refused anyway
category_name: Visas, refusals and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The stated grounds are usually that the officer is not satisfied the applicant will leave. That is a prediction about the future, it cannot be disproved with documents, and it is not appealable in most categories.

title: The agent who filled in your form
category_name: Visas, refusals and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Where the process is opaque and the stakes are high, an industry of agents appears. Some are useful, many are extractive, and a few enter information the applicant has never seen - which the applicant is then held responsible for.

title: A passport that ranks 90th and shrinks
category_name: The passport, the booklet racket and proving who you are
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The Nigerian passport reaches 44 destinations without a prior visa. The number has been falling, and the long-run trend is downward against peers.

title: The booklet that is not there
category_name: The passport, the booklet racket and proving who you are
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Getting the passport at all is a hurdle before it is used. Booklets run short, the portal shows 'processing' for months, and the people who pay privately are served first.

title: Proving you are who you say, repeatedly
category_name: The passport, the booklet racket and proving who you are
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Identity in Nigeria is assembled from several partial systems - NIN, BVN, voter card, driver's licence, certificate of origin - none of which is sufficient alone, and each of which requires the others.

title: Documents that are assumed to be forged
category_name: The passport, the booklet racket and proving who you are
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Nigerian civil and academic documents attract verification demands that documents from other countries do not, at the applicant's cost and on the applicant's time.

title: The second room
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks about unusually high rates of random checks. The honest position: the mechanics are documented, the referral criteria are published in outline, and no government publishes a per-nationality secondary-inspection rate - so the disparity is attested by consistent reporting rather than by a statistic.

title: Deportation, and the third country
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Removal is not only to Nigeria. Third-country arrangements mean a Nigerian removed from one state may be delivered to another entirely.

title: Being the nationality the airline worries about
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Carriers bear fines for bringing inadmissible passengers, so they screen before departure - which moves part of the border to the check-in desk in Lagos.

title: The exit interview at your own departure
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Leaving Nigeria involves its own layers - immigration, security, sometimes a trafficking screening that is necessary in design and intrusive in execution, and which falls hardest on young women travelling alone.

title: Refused entry with valid documents
category_name: Borders, entry refusals and being turned around
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A visa is permission to ask. Documented cases show Nigerians with valid visas, return tickets, accommodation and funds refused entry, detained for days, and removed - sometimes to a third country.

title: Refused for travelling without a man
category_name: Borders, entry refusals and being turned around
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The clearest single intersection in this dataset: a state refused entry to hundreds of Nigerian women, not for anything about them, but because they arrived without a husband or male relative.

title: Coming home, and the desk at that end too
category_name: Borders, entry refusals and being turned around
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Return is not frictionless either. Arrival in Nigeria involves its own informal costs, and for deportees and returnees a reception that is administrative rather than supportive.

title: Claiming asylum from a country nobody calls a war
category_name: Status abroad: asylum, deportation and the years in between
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Nigeria is not at war in the way decision-makers picture, so a Nigerian claim starts from a presumption of safety and must dismantle it - which is a different and harder task than arriving from a recognised conflict.

title: Germany: refused, and deported to Italy
category_name: Status abroad: asylum, deportation and the years in between
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The Dublin system means a Nigerian claim in Germany is frequently not decided on its merits at all, but declared inadmissible and routed to the first EU country of entry - and if that transfer fails, the clock restarts.

title: The years with no status and no exit
category_name: Status abroad: asylum, deportation and the years in between
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Between refusal and removal there is a condition with no name: not lawful, not removable, not permitted to work, and not permitted to leave and return.

title: Regularising, and the fee that is the barrier
category_name: Status abroad: asylum, deportation and the years in between
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Where a route to status exists, it is priced - and the price is set at a level that functions as the actual eligibility criterion.

title: Being read as a fraud before you speak
category_name: The 419 inheritance: being read as a fraud before you speak
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: No other nationality in this set of datasets carries a scam as its global shorthand. 'Nigerian prince' is a punchline in languages that have no other Nigerian referent, and it arrives in the room before the person does.

title: Yahoo boys, and the men who are not them
category_name: The 419 inheritance: being read as a fraud before you speak
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The domestic term for internet fraudsters has become an international descriptor for young Nigerian men generally, including the overwhelming majority who are not involved.

title: Guilty until verified, at every institution
category_name: The 419 inheritance: being read as a fraud before you speak
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The reputational default converts into procedure: more documents, more checks, longer holds, and a higher bar for the same transaction.

title: What it does to a person to be a punchline
category_name: The 419 inheritance: being read as a fraud before you speak
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Distinct from the economic cost: the internal effect of belonging to a nationality that is a globally recognised joke about dishonesty.

title: Twenty years without PayPal
category_name: Banking, cards and payment exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: From 2004 to 2026 Nigerians could not receive money through the world's default consumer payment platform. The exclusion was explicit, national, and outlasted the conditions given for it.

title: The card that stops working at the border
category_name: Banking, cards and payment exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: About 120 million payment cards circulate in Nigeria and the overwhelming majority cannot be used abroad or online internationally - by design of the domestic rails and by bank-imposed ceilings.

title: Remittance in, difficulty out
category_name: Banking, cards and payment exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Money flows into Nigeria at scale and with official encouragement. Money flowing out, or being received by a Nigerian business from abroad, meets a different regime entirely.

title: Being de-risked as a category
category_name: Banking, cards and payment exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Compliance departments manage country risk by declining the country. The individual customer is never assessed, and never told that is what happened.

title: Being blocked for where your IP says you are
category_name: Geoblocking, platforms and digital redlining
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Merchants and platforms exclude Nigeria at the network level. The block is national in scope, trivially evaded by the people it targets, and binding on everyone who is not trying to evade anything.

title: Platforms that flag you by default
category_name: Geoblocking, platforms and digital redlining
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Freelance marketplaces, marketplaces and social platforms apply elevated scrutiny to Nigerian accounts, with suspension arriving before any explanation.

title: The internet costs more and works less
category_name: Geoblocking, platforms and digital redlining
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Before any discrimination, the connection itself is expensive relative to income, unreliable, and dependent on the power supply in PWR-001.

title: Kidnapping as an industry
category_name: Insecurity: kidnapping, banditry and armed groups
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: What began as ideological abduction became a ransom business with a price list. It is low-risk, lucrative, and now operates across most of the country rather than one corner of it.

title: Taking the schoolchildren
category_name: Insecurity: kidnapping, banditry and armed groups
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Mass school abduction became a repeatable tactic after 2014. The specific consequence is that education itself becomes a risk calculation, and it is calculated differently for daughters.

title: Being displaced inside your own country
category_name: Insecurity: kidnapping, banditry and armed groups
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Millions have left home without crossing a border, which means no refugee status, no agency mandate, and frequently no camp - just another poor village absorbing people it cannot feed.

title: The security you have to buy
category_name: Insecurity: kidnapping, banditry and armed groups
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Where the state does not provide protection, households and businesses purchase it - which makes safety an income-tiered product and leaves everyone else with the risk.

title: The checkpoint that wants twenty naira
category_name: Police, extortion and what happened at Lekki
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Routine police extortion is a small, constant, unavoidable levy on movement, and refusing it is more expensive than paying.

title: What happened at Lekki
category_name: Police, extortion and what happened at Lekki
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: The clearest documented case of the state using lethal force on its own unarmed citizens in this dataset - established by a judicial panel, denied by the government, and unpunished.

title: Reporting a crime as a woman
category_name: Police, extortion and what happened at Lekki
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The institution that would record a sexual or domestic offence is frequently the one that dissuades, mocks, charges a fee, or suggests the family settle it.

title: The grid that goes off, nationally
category_name: Electricity, fuel and the generator economy
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Not outages in the ordinary sense. The national grid collapses entirely, repeatedly, and everything downstream of electricity is built around the assumption that it will.

title: Paying for darkness
category_name: Electricity, fuel and the generator economy
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: More than half of registered electricity customers have no meter, so they are billed by estimate - and the estimates are systematically wrong in one direction.

title: The morning the fuel price doubled
category_name: Inflation, subsidy removal and the cost of an ordinary month
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: On 29 May 2023 the fuel subsidy was removed in a sentence, and the price of moving anything - people, food, goods - repriced within weeks.

title: Running a household at 34% inflation
category_name: Inflation, subsidy removal and the cost of an ordinary month
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The management of a shrinking budget against rising prices is daily, skilled, unpaid work, and it is overwhelmingly done by women.

title: Being paid in a currency that is leaving
category_name: Inflation, subsidy removal and the cost of an ordinary month
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Naira earnings against dollar-denominated costs - school fees abroad, software, medical treatment, imported goods - means a salary that falls in real terms without anyone cutting it.

title: A health system with a third of its doctors licensed elsewhere
category_name: The health system, and the people who left it
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Nigeria trains health workers and then loses them, at a rate that has converted a staffing problem into a structural one.

title: Japa: the exit as a national event
category_name: The health system, and the people who left it
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Emigration of skilled workers is not a trickle or an aspiration. It is measurable in the destination countries' own registration data, and the health sector is where it is most visible.

title: Being treated abroad, and being suspected there
category_name: The health system, and the people who left it
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Nigerian patients and Nigerian-trained clinicians abroad both encounter a presumption - of health tourism in one direction, of inadequate training in the other.

title: One of the most dangerous places in the world to give birth
category_name: Maternal health, obstructed labour and fistula
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Nigeria carries a share of global maternal deaths far out of proportion to its population, and the northern ratio is several times the national one.

title: Obstetric fistula: the injury of waiting too long
category_name: Maternal health, obstructed labour and fistula
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Prolonged obstructed labour without a caesarean produces an injury that is preventable, repairable, and in Nigeria enormously common - and it ends the woman's social life as reliably as it damages her body.

title: Deciding whether to have a child at all
category_name: Maternal health, obstructed labour and fistula
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Contraception, spacing and the number of pregnancies are frequently not the woman's decision to make, which converts every other maternal risk into a recurring one.

title: The cost of a delivery, in cash, on the night
category_name: Maternal health, obstructed labour and fistula
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Facility delivery is priced and paid at the point of use, which makes the safest option the one that requires money to be available at 2am.

title: The bills that were rejected
category_name: Women's legal status: marriage, inheritance, the bills that failed
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Nigeria's legislature has repeatedly declined to pass gender equality provisions. The refusals are recent, recorded, and are the reason several other issues in this dataset have no remedy.

title: Being an indigene of nowhere
category_name: Women's legal status: marriage, inheritance, the bills that failed
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Indigeneship determines access to scholarships, state employment, quotas and land. It follows birth, not marriage - so a married woman is frequently treated as belonging to neither state.

title: Married before eighteen
category_name: Women's legal status: marriage, inheritance, the bills that failed
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: A third of Nigerian girls marry before 18, and in several northern states it is nearly two thirds. The constitutional provision that would have settled the age contains a clause that undoes it.

title: Inheriting, in theory
category_name: Women's legal status: marriage, inheritance, the bills that failed
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The Supreme Court held in 2014 that customary law barring daughters from inheriting is unconstitutional. Twelve years on, most people affected have not heard of the judgment and compliance is very low.

title: Being a widow
category_name: Women's legal status: marriage, inheritance, the bills that failed
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Widowhood in much of Nigeria triggers a set of practices that strip property, restrict movement and impose ritual humiliation - enforced by the husband's family and frequently by other women.

title: Cutting
category_name: The body: cutting, widowhood rites and what is done to it
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Female genital mutilation is prohibited by federal law that applies directly in one federal territory, prohibited by state law in thirteen states, and practised in the regions where prevalence is highest.

title: Whose body it is treated as
category_name: The body: cutting, widowhood rites and what is done to it
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Across marriage, health and inheritance law the recurring structure is that decisions about a woman's body are made with reference to a man's position.

title: Menstruation, and what it costs to manage
category_name: The body: cutting, widowhood rites and what is done to it
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Products, privacy, water and disposal are all purchased or absent, and where they are absent the consequence is measured in school days.

title: Being visible in public as a woman
category_name: The body: cutting, widowhood rites and what is done to it
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Street harassment, transport harassment and the assumption of availability are a continuous tax on moving through public space.

title: Benin City to Italy
category_name: Trafficking, the Gulf, and being sent somewhere and left
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: One city in Edo State became the main hub for sex trafficking between West Africa and Europe. The route is documented, the debt is priced, and the binding mechanism is an oath.

title: The Gulf contract
category_name: Trafficking, the Gulf, and being sent somewhere and left
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Recruited legally as a housekeeper, flown out with a signed contract, and then unable to leave the country without the employer's permission. The brief calls this being sent somewhere and dumped; the legal name is kafala.

title: Knowing, and going anyway
category_name: Trafficking, the Gulf, and being sent somewhere and left
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Awareness campaigns assume the women do not know. Many do. The decision is made against the alternatives available at home, and the alternatives are the rest of this dataset.

title: Being suspected of being trafficked
category_name: Trafficking, the Gulf, and being sent somewhere and left
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The mirror of TRF-001: because the route is well documented, young Nigerian women travelling legitimately are screened, doubted and delayed on suspicion of being victims.

title: A university year that does not happen
category_name: Education, strikes and a certificate nobody abroad trusts
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Public university teaching stops for months at a time. Students are not taught, not examined, not graduated, and not compensated.

title: The children who are not in school
category_name: Education, strikes and a certificate nobody abroad trusts
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Nigeria holds one of the largest out-of-school populations in the world, and the majority of those children are girls.

title: A certificate that is discounted abroad
category_name: Education, strikes and a certificate nobody abroad trusts
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Nigerian qualifications attract verification, equivalency downgrades and outright scepticism - a discount applied to the document rather than the holder.

title: NYSC, and a year the state assigns you
category_name: Education, strikes and a certificate nobody abroad trusts
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: The National Youth Service Corps posts graduates for a year to a state not of their choosing, and completion is required for much formal employment.

title: Sex for grades
category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The transaction is well enough known to have a name, and it was documented on camera at two of the region's most prestigious universities.

title: The workplace version
category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The same structure moves into employment: a man with discretion over hiring, confirmation, promotion or payment, and no functioning complaint route.

title: Being harassed and being the one who is judged
category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Disclosure carries a reputational cost to the woman, which is why prevalence is understated everywhere including in this dataset.

title: The statistics that say there is no problem
category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Nigeria's headline unemployment rate is around 4%, which is lower than Germany's. The number is not wrong; it is measuring something other than what people mean by unemployment.

title: Working informally, which is most people
category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: 93% of employment is informal, which means no contract, no pension, no sick pay, no maternity provision, and no mechanism when something goes wrong.

title: The name on the CV, abroad
category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Before any question of qualifications, the name on the application changes the callback probability - which is one of the best-evidenced findings in labour economics.

title: What a woman's work is assumed to be
category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: High female self-employment and informality are read as entrepreneurial culture. They are the residue of exclusion from formal work.

title: A name the form cannot hold
category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Nigerian names are long, tonal, frequently multi-part, and carry diacritics that systems strip. The result is a person whose documents do not agree with each other, through nobody's error.

title: The identity is frozen before you reach the airport
category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Air travel locks a vetted identity at booking. A mismatch found later cannot be fixed at the desk by anyone, for technical reasons rather than unhelpfulness.

title: Sharing a name with somebody
category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Name-based screening produces false positives, and clearing one is not a thing that can be done once.

title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A large share of the hurdles in this dataset are not policy. They are one person's decision on one day, which another person would have made differently, and which is then permanent.

title: The error that becomes your record
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A wrong date, spelling or status code entered once is copied forward by every later system, and the burden of disproving it is entirely the person's.

title: The file nobody can find
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Verification in Nigeria frequently depends on a physical record held by an institution with no functioning archive, and the absence is treated as the applicant's problem.

title: Being read as dishonest before you speak
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks for the psychological effects of being seen as bad. For Nigerians the content of the stereotype is specifically dishonesty, which means the suspicion attaches to the person's word rather than to their capability.

title: The relationship market, with the nationality priced in
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief names this directly. The identity changes who will partner with you, on what terms, and how the relationship is read by everyone around it - and the romance-scam association gives it a specific and unusually corrosive content.

title: Not being able to plan
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Currency movement, power failure, insecurity and administrative unpredictability together remove the assumption of continuity that any long project requires.

title: The arithmetic that never stops
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: Running a household under ECO-002 is continuous mental computation - prices, credit, who is owed, what can wait - and it occupies the same capacity that would otherwise go to work or study.

title: The one who left, and the one who stayed
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Japa splits families into senders and receivers, and the remittance relationship carries obligation, guilt and quiet resentment in both directions.

title: What it takes out of the work
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks specifically about efficiency and growth. The costs are real, large, and attributed to the person rather than to the conditions in essentially every setting.

title: Back pain, and the fact that it is measured
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: The brief asks about back pain specifically. It is not a figure of speech: Nigeria may carry one of the heaviest low back pain burdens in the world, and the rural figure is roughly double the urban one.

title: The stress of running a household, in the spine
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
summary: The single most directly relevant finding in this dataset to what the brief asked: Nigerian women who appraised their domestic responsibilities as very stressful had roughly three times the odds of low back pain.

title: Depression, arriving as a physical complaint
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
summary: Psychological distress in Nigeria commonly presents somatically, which means it is investigated as a physical problem, not found, and the patient is left believing nobody could identify what is wrong.

title: The productivity loss nobody has quantified
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks about effects on efficiency and growth. The honest position is that the components are well evidenced and the total is not, because the study joining them has not been done.
